docs.title: How to test
docs.text:
Directly against account, without the gateway (for example with kubectl port-forward svc/account 8080 or by exposing the port in compose):

curl -i -X POST localhost:8080/accounts -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Ana","email":"ana@insper.edu.br","password":"segredo123"}'
# HTTP/1.1 201  Location: http://localhost:8080/accounts/<id>

curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/accounts/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"ana@insper.edu.br","password":"segredo123"}'
# {"id":"<id>","name":"Ana","email":"ana@insper.edu.br"}

For the whole platform, scripts/smoke-test.sh signs up, logs in and calls /accounts through the gateway.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Owner: Nicolas · Repositories: pna26/auth (interface) and pna26/auth-service (implementation)

Auth handles the user's identity. It:

  1. signs up users (POST /auth/register), forwarding to Account;
  2. handles login (POST /auth/login): asks Account to check the email and password and, if they match, generates a JWT and returns it in the __store_jwt_token cookie;
  3. resolves the token for the gateway (POST /auth/solve): checks the signature and validity and returns the account id;
  4. returns the logged-in user's data (GET /auth/me) and handles logout (deletes the cookie).

Auth has no database: Account stores the accounts and password hashes. It is a Spring Boot (Web MVC) + OpenFeign service, with the JWT built by the JJWT 0.13 library. It follows hands-on 3 of the course.

docs.title: Two repositories: interface and implementation
docs.text:
Repository Contents Used by auth AuthController (interface with the routes and the cookie name) and the DTOs RegisterIn, LoginIn and TokenOut auth-service (implements it) auth-service AuthResource, AuthService, JwtService, Dockerfile and k8s/ becomes the auth-service image

auth-service also depends on the Account interface (store:account:1.0.0) and uses it as a Feign client (@EnableFeignClients(basePackages = "store.account")): calling Account is calling a Java method, and Feign turns it into POST http://account:8080/accounts/login.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text: Method Route Input Output Token at the gateway? POST /auth/register { name, email, password } 200 no POST /auth/login { email, password } 200 + Set-Cookie: __store_jwt_token=<jwt> or 401 no GET /auth/logout — 200 + empty cookie with Max-Age=0 no GET /auth/me id-account header (set by the gateway) { id, name, email } yes POST /auth/solve { token } { idAccount } or 401 only the gateway calls it, internally GET /auth/health-check — 200 yes

docs.title: Login and token usage
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as User
    participant G as gateway
    participant A as auth
    participant C as account
    U->>G: POST /auth/login {email, password}
    G->>A: (open route)
    A->>C: POST /accounts/login (Feign)
    C-->>A: {id, name, email} or 401
    A->>A: signed JWT (HMAC-SHA256)
    A-->>U: 200 Set-Cookie: __store_jwt_token
    U->>G: GET /accounts (cookie)
    G->>A: POST /auth/solve {token}
    A->>A: checks signature, nbf and exp
    A-->>G: {idAccount}
    G->>C: GET /accounts + id-account

The gateway stores the /auth/solve result in Redis for a few minutes (see Cache), so Auth is not called on every request.

docs.title: JWT
docs.text:
Field Value jti (id) account id: this is what /auth/solve returns sub account name email account email iss Insper::PMA nbf / exp now / now + JWT_DURATION Signature HMAC-SHA256 with the JWT_SECRET_KEY key (base64 of 32 bytes)

The token carries no password and is not encrypted (anyone can decode its base64 content); what prevents forgery is the signature. Any change to the token, or a token signed with another key, makes parseSignedClaims fail and /auth/solve respond 401. The same applies to an expired token.

docs.title: Cookie
docs.text:
Attribute Why HttpOnly the page's JavaScript cannot read the cookie, so an XSS cannot steal the token Secure the browser only sends the cookie over HTTPS (or to localhost) SameSite=None lets a front end on another origin call the API with the cookie (requires Secure) Path=/, Max-Age = token duration the cookie applies to all routes and expires along with the token

Secure is why the browser does not store the cookie on EKS, which currently serves only over HTTP: see HTTPS (known limitation).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason Auth without a database, checking the password in Account A single owner of account data. Auth never sees the hash: it sends the password to Account and receives only { id, name, email }. Stateless JWT Validation does not need a database lookup, only the key. Any Auth replica validates any token. Wrong login → 401 AuthService converts Account's 401/400 (which arrives as a FeignException) into 401 Invalid credentials. Invalid token → 401, no stack trace JwtService catches the JwtException and responds 401; the gateway treats a 4xx from solve as "not authenticated". JWT_SECRET_KEY required There is no default key in the code: without the variable, Auth does not start. A key in the public repository would let anyone generate valid tokens. In compose it comes from .env (scripts/build.sh generates a random one); on EKS, from the auth-secrets Secret. JJWT pinned version (0.13.0) The JJWT API changed a lot between versions (parserBuilder → parser().verifyWith); with a pinned version the build does not break on its own.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Limitation How it would look in production An Account error during sign-up (e.g. duplicate email, short password) reaches the user as 500 handle the FeignException in create and forward Account's status (400, 409) GET /auth/me with an id that no longer exists (deleted account, token still valid) returns 500 forward Account's 404 Logout only deletes the cookie: the token remains valid until exp if someone has a copy revoked token list (by jti) in Redis, checked by the gateway No roles (every logged-in user can do everything) done: role claim in the JWT and check in the gateway, see Authorization (RBAC)

docs.title: Code
Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default in code Compose EKS Purpose JWT_SECRET_KEY — (required) .env Secret auth-secrets JWT HMAC key, base64 of 32 bytes (openssl rand -base64 32) JWT_DURATION 3600000 (1 h) 86400000 (24 h) 3600000 (1 h) token and cookie validity, in milliseconds JWT_HTTP_ONLY true true true cookie HttpOnly attribute

docs.title: How to test
docs.text:
Through the gateway (compose at http://localhost):

curl -s -X POST localhost/auth/register -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Ana","email":"ana@insper.edu.br","password":"segredo123"}'

curl -si -X POST localhost/auth/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"ana@insper.edu.br","password":"segredo123"}' | grep -i set-cookie
# set-cookie: __store_jwt_token=eyJ...; Path=/; Max-Age=86400; ...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None

curl -s localhost/auth/me -H "Cookie: __store_jwt_token=eyJ..."
# {"id":"...","name":"Ana","email":"ana@insper.edu.br"}

A tampered token (change a letter in the middle) makes /auth/me respond 401, because the signature no longer matches. scripts/smoke-test.sh repeats this flow against compose or the EKS ELB.

docs.title: Exchange
docs.text:
Owner: Gabriel — repository pna26/exchange-service

Currency exchange microservice in Python (FastAPI). It receives a currency pair, fetches the exchange rate from the Central Bank's PTAX (BACEN's Olinda API, public and with no sign-up) and returns the buy and sell price to the logged-in user. It follows the BACEN service suggested by the professor: the free exchange rate APIs (AwesomeAPI, used before) do not respond to AWS IPs, and on EKS they returned 429 for the NAT IP.

Status (20/11/2026)

The PTAX implementation is in pna26/exchange-service#1 (44 tests passing), waiting for the repository owner to merge it. Until then, the code tabs below and the deployed service are the previous version (AwesomeAPI); this page already describes the new one.

flowchart LR
    u([User]) -->|"GET /exchange/USD/BRL<br/>JWT cookie"| lb[lb · Nginx] --> gw[gateway]
    gw -->|"+ id-account header"| ex[exchange]
    ex <-->|"hit (30 s)"| cache[(in-memory cache)]
    ex -->|"miss"| api([PTAX · BACEN])

docs.title: Contract
How the rate is calculated
docs.text:
For each currency, the service queries CotacaoMoedaPeriodo over a 7-day window (weekends and holidays have no quote) and uses the last bulletin in the list. PTAX only quotes currency → BRL, so the real is worth 1 and any pair is computed as a cross rate via BRL, with c = buy and v = sell in BRL:

sell = v(from) / c(to) · buy = c(from) / v(to) (6 decimal places)

There are 10 currencies (AUD, CAD, CHF, DKK, EUR, GBP, JPY, NOK, SEK and USD, plus BRL). Real call on 20/11/2026: USD/BRL → sell 5.8889, buy 5.8883 (bulletin of 19/11 13:04); USD/EUR → sell 0.910763, buy 0.910487.

PTAX limits

  • Bulletins only exist on business days, between ≈ 10h and 13h (Brasília time): outside that window the response is the last published bulletin, not a real-time exchange rate.
  • It is a public BCB service: do not load test it. The cache is always on; in a load test k6 hits memory (count the X-Cache: miss).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason FastAPI + async httpx While waiting for the external API, the process serves other requests (the service is almost pure I/O). BACEN PTAX as provider (EXCHANGE_PROVIDER=ptax) Public, no key, responds to AWS IPs (AwesomeAPI returned 429 on EKS). Sell → sell, buy → buy (hence sell ≥ buy). AwesomeAPI only as an option (EXCHANGE_PROVIDER=awesomeapi) The old mode is still available, with PTAX as fallback when AwesomeAPI fails (EXCHANGE_FALLBACK). pip + requirements.txt, not uv The course guide uses uv; the reusable platform pipeline installs Python dependencies with pip, so we kept the same Dockerfile. Exchange rate cache for 30 s This is this service's bottleneck: see Exchange rate cache. Same currency (BRL/BRL) returns 1.0 without calling PTAX Avoids a pointless external call. 401 without id-account The service should only be reached through the gateway; without the header, the request came from somewhere else. 1 uvicorn process per container prometheus_client metrics live in process memory; with several workers each scrape would see a different one. Scales with replicas (EXCHANGE_REPLICAS / replicas in k8s). Port 8080 and name exchange The gateway forwards to http://exchange:8080 in compose and k8s. /metrics outside /exchange/** The gateway only forwards /exchange/**, so metrics stay on the internal network only (Prometheus scrapes directly). python:3.12-slim image, user 1001, read-only FS in k8s Fewer packages for Trivy and the same security pattern as the other services.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default EXCHANGE_PROVIDER ptax ptax or awesomeapi PTAX_URL https://olinda.bcb.gov.br/olinda/servico/PTAX/versao/v1/odata BACEN PTAX API CACHE_TTL 30 seconds an exchange rate is valid (0 disables the cache) CACHE_STALE_TTL 600 how long the last exchange rate is served if PTAX goes down UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT 3 timeout of external calls, in seconds EXCHANGE_API_URL https://economia.awesomeapi.com.br/json/last awesomeapi mode only EXCHANGE_API_TOKEN — awesomeapi mode only (optional) EXCHANGE_FALLBACK ptax awesomeapi mode only: uses PTAX if AwesomeAPI fails (none disables it)

The exchange_upstream_request_seconds{outcome} metric (Grafana "External API" panel) measures the main provider, so it now shows the calls to PTAX; a pair without BRL (USD/EUR) makes two calls.

In compose, EXCHANGE_CACHE_TTL and EXCHANGE_REPLICAS (in .env) become CACHE_TTL and the number of replicas.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
app/main.pyapp/provider.pyapp/cache.pyDockerfilek8s/k8s.yaml 
"""Exchange: cotação entre moedas para usuários autenticados.

Contrato (docs/arquitetura.md do platform):

    GET /exchange/{from}/{to}     header id-account (injetado pelo gateway)
    -> { "sell": float, "buy": float, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", "id-account": "..." }

A cotação vem de uma API de terceiros (AwesomeAPI). Bottleneck tratado aqui:
cada chamada externa custa ~100-500 ms e a API tem limite de requisições, então
guardamos a cotação em memória por CACHE_TTL segundos (ver cache.py).
"""

import os
import re
import time
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

import httpx
from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException, Request, Response
from prometheus_client import CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST, Histogram, generate_latest
from starlette.routing import Match

from .cache import QuoteCache
from .provider import AwesomeApiProvider, PairNotFound, UpstreamError

CURRENCY = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]{3}$")

HTTP_SECONDS = Histogram(
    "exchange_http_server_requests_seconds",
    "Tempo de resposta das rotas do exchange",
    ["method", "route", "status"],
    buckets=(0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5),
)


def create_app(transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    """Fábrica do app. Os testes passam um transport falso no lugar da API externa."""

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
        timeout = float(os.getenv("UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT", "3"))
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout, transport=transport) as client:
            provider = AwesomeApiProvider(
                client,
                base_url=os.getenv("EXCHANGE_API_URL", "https://economia.awesomeapi.com.br/json/last"),
                token=os.getenv("EXCHANGE_API_TOKEN") or None,
            )
            app.state.cache = QuoteCache(
                provider.fetch,
                ttl=float(os.getenv("CACHE_TTL", "30")),
                stale_ttl=float(os.getenv("CACHE_STALE_TTL", "600")),
            )
            yield

    app = FastAPI(title="exchange", lifespan=lifespan, docs_url="/exchange/docs",
                  openapi_url="/exchange/openapi.json", redoc_url=None)

    @app.middleware("http")
    async def metrics_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        status = 500
        try:
            response = await call_next(request)
            status = response.status_code
            return response
        finally:
            # usa o template da rota ("/exchange/{from_}/{to}") e não a URL real,
            # para não criar uma série no Prometheus por par de moedas
            path = next((r.path for r in app.routes if r.matches(request.scope)[0] == Match.FULL), "desconhecida")
            if path != "/metrics":
                HTTP_SECONDS.labels(request.method, path, str(status)).observe(time.perf_counter() - start)

    @app.get("/exchange/health-check")
    @app.get("/health")
    async def health():
        return {"status": "UP"}

    @app.get("/metrics", include_in_schema=False)
    async def metrics():
        # só na rede interna: o gateway só encaminha /exchange/** e o lb não expõe o exchange
        return Response(generate_latest(), media_type=CONTENT_TYPE_LATEST)

    @app.get("/exchange/{from_}/{to}")
    async def exchange(
        from_: str,
        to: str,
        request: Request,
        id_account: str | None = Header(default=None, alias="id-account"),
    ):
        # o gateway sempre injeta o id-account depois de validar o JWT; sem ele a
        # requisição não passou pelo gateway
        if not id_account:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="header id-account ausente")
        if not CURRENCY.match(from_) or not CURRENCY.match(to):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="moeda deve ter 3 letras (ISO 4217), ex.: USD")

        src, dst = from_.upper(), to.upper()
        if src == dst:
            return {"sell": 1.0, "buy": 1.0, "date": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "id-account": id_account}

        try:
            quote = await request.app.state.cache.get(src, dst)
        except PairNotFound:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"par {src}-{dst} não suportado")
        except UpstreamError:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="API de câmbio indisponível, tente de novo")

        return {"sell": quote.sell, "buy": quote.buy, "date": quote.date, "id-account": id_account}

    return app


app = create_app()

"""Cliente da API de câmbio de terceiros (AwesomeAPI, gratuita e sem cadastro).

    GET https://economia.awesomeapi.com.br/json/last/USD-BRL
    -> {"USDBRL": {"bid": "5.39", "ask": "5.40", "create_date": "2026-11-05 10:00:00", ...}}

"bid" é o preço pelo qual o mercado compra a moeda (buy) e "ask" o preço pelo
qual vende (sell); por isso sell >= buy.
"""

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass

import httpx
from prometheus_client import Histogram

UPSTREAM_SECONDS = Histogram(
    "exchange_upstream_request_seconds",
    "Tempo das chamadas à API de câmbio externa",
    ["outcome"],
    buckets=(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5),
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Quote:
    sell: float
    buy: float
    date: str


class PairNotFound(Exception):
    """A API externa não conhece o par de moedas."""


class UpstreamError(Exception):
    """A API externa falhou (timeout, 5xx, limite de requisições, resposta inválida)."""


class AwesomeApiProvider:
    def __init__(self, client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str, token: str | None = None):
        self._client = client
        self._base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._token = token

    async def fetch(self, src: str, dst: str) -> Quote:
        params = {"token": self._token} if self._token else None
        start = time.perf_counter()
        outcome = "error"
        try:
            try:
                resp = await self._client.get(f"{self._base_url}/{src}-{dst}", params=params)
            except httpx.HTTPError as e:
                raise UpstreamError(str(e)) from e

            if resp.status_code == 404:
                outcome = "not_found"
                raise PairNotFound(f"{src}-{dst}")
            if resp.status_code != 200:
                raise UpstreamError(f"status {resp.status_code}")

            try:
                data = resp.json()[f"{src}{dst}"]
                quote = Quote(sell=float(data["ask"]), buy=float(data["bid"]), date=data["create_date"])
            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
                raise UpstreamError(f"resposta inesperada: {e}") from e

            outcome = "ok"
            return quote
        finally:
            UPSTREAM_SECONDS.labels(outcome).observe(time.perf_counter() - start)

"""Bottleneck: cache da cotação.

Sem cache, cada GET /exchange/USD/BRL vira uma chamada HTTP para a API externa:
latência de rede de terceiros no caminho de toda requisição e risco de bater no
limite de requisições da API (que derruba o serviço para todo mundo).

Decisões:
  - cache em memória por par, TTL curto (CACHE_TTL, padrão 30 s): cotação de
    30 s atrás é aceitável para uma loja, e a cardinalidade é minúscula
    (poucos pares de moedas), então não precisa de Redis;
  - um lock por par: com 200 usuários pedindo USD-BRL no mesmo instante em que
    o cache expira, só UMA chamada vai para a API externa (evita "cache stampede");
  - se a API externa falhar, devolve a última cotação conhecida por até
    CACHE_STALE_TTL (padrão 10 min) em vez de 503 ("stale-if-error").
"""

import asyncio
import time
from typing import Awaitable, Callable

from prometheus_client import Counter

from .provider import PairNotFound, Quote, UpstreamError

CACHE_RESULTS = Counter(
    "exchange_quote_cache",
    "Resultado da consulta ao cache de cotações",
    ["result"],  # hit | miss | stale | error
)

Fetcher = Callable[[str, str], Awaitable[Quote]]


class QuoteCache:
    def __init__(self, fetch: Fetcher, ttl: float, stale_ttl: float, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic):
        self._fetch = fetch
        self._ttl = ttl
        self._stale_ttl = stale_ttl
        self._clock = clock
        self._entries: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Quote, float]] = {}
        self._locks: dict[tuple[str, str], asyncio.Lock] = {}

    def _fresh(self, key: tuple[str, str]) -> Quote | None:
        entry = self._entries.get(key)
        if entry and self._clock() - entry[1] < self._ttl:
            return entry[0]
        return None

    async def get(self, src: str, dst: str) -> Quote:
        key = (src, dst)
        if self._ttl > 0 and (quote := self._fresh(key)):
            CACHE_RESULTS.labels("hit").inc()
            return quote

        lock = self._locks.setdefault(key, asyncio.Lock())
        async with lock:
            # outra requisição pode ter atualizado o cache enquanto esperávamos o lock
            if self._ttl > 0 and (quote := self._fresh(key)):
                CACHE_RESULTS.labels("hit").inc()
                return quote

            try:
                quote = await self._fetch(src, dst)
            except PairNotFound:
                CACHE_RESULTS.labels("miss").inc()
                raise
            except UpstreamError:
                entry = self._entries.get(key)
                if entry and self._clock() - entry[1] < self._stale_ttl:
                    CACHE_RESULTS.labels("stale").inc()
                    return entry[0]
                CACHE_RESULTS.labels("error").inc()
                raise

            CACHE_RESULTS.labels("miss").inc()
            self._entries[key] = (quote, self._clock())
            return quote

# imagem slim: menos pacotes do SO para o Trivy apontar como vulneráveis
FROM python:3.12-slim

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1

WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

COPY app ./app

# não roda como root (mesmo uid dos outros serviços nos manifestos k8s)
RUN groupadd --system app && useradd --system --gid app --uid 1001 app
USER 1001

EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --retries=3 \
  CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8080/health', timeout=2)"

# 1 processo por container: as métricas do prometheus_client ficam na memória
# do processo, e com vários workers cada scrape veria um worker diferente.

The smoke test checks the route end to end through the gateway, including that the incoming id-account is the logged-in user's.

Verified on 20/11/2026: 44 tests passing; service running locally against the real PTAX (USD/BRL → 200 with X-Cache: miss and then hit, XYZ/BRL → 404, no id-account → 401). Earlier, on 05/11/2026, with AwesomeAPI: 21 tests; service running against the real AwesomeAPI (200 with sell ≥ buy for USD/BRL and EUR/BRL, correct 400, 401 and 404); full smoke test on the local platform (GET /exchange/USD/BRL → 200 with the user's id-account). Performance in the load test and in Exchange rate cache.

External API in CI and on EKS

With AwesomeAPI, the GitHub Actions runner and the EKS NAT got an error (429) and Exchange returned 503 (the smoke test treats this as a warning). That is why we switched to PTAX. Still to be confirmed from AWS: from a cluster pod, curl the PTAX URL once (a step in the course guide) and GET /exchange/USD/BRL through the ELB.

cd api/exchange-service
pip install -r requirements.txt pytest && pytest -q

docs.title: Gateway
docs.text:
Owner: Leonardo · Repository: pna26/gateway-service

The gateway is the platform's single entry point. It:

  1. routes each path to the right microservice (/auth/**, /accounts/**, /exchange/**);
  2. authorizes: on every route that is not open, it requires the __store_jwt_token cookie, validates the token with Auth (POST /auth/solve) and forwards the account id in the id-account header;
  3. drops any id-account sent by the client, so nobody can impersonate another account;
  4. stores the token validation result in Redis (cache bottleneck);
  5. exposes GET /health-check with the replica's hostname (shows the load balancing).

It is built with Spring Cloud Gateway on top of WebFlux (reactive), as in hands-on 2 and 3 of the course.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Path Destination Token? POST /auth/register, POST /auth/login, GET /auth/logout auth:8080 no other /auth/** auth:8080 yes /accounts/** account:8080 yes /exchange/** exchange:8080 yes /exchanges/** exchange:8080, rewritten to /exchange/** yes GET /health-check the gateway itself no /gateway/actuator/health, /gateway/actuator/prometheus the gateway itself no (lb blocks prometheus from outside)

Destinations come from environment variables (AUTH_URI, ACCOUNT_URI, EXCHANGE_URI), defaulting to the compose/k8s service names.

docs.title: Authorization decision
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Request] --> B{open route?<br/>RouterValidator}
    B -- yes --> OK[forward to service]
    B -- no --> C{cookie<br/>__store_jwt_token?}
    C -- no --> E401[401]
    C -- yes --> D{token in Redis?}
    D -- yes --> H[header id-account = cached id]
    D -- no --> F[POST /auth/solve]
    F -- 4xx --> E401
    F -- error/timeout --> E503[503]
    F -- 200 --> G[store in Redis<br/>TTL = min 5 min, exp]
    G --> H
    H --> OK

Differences from the hands-on 3 code:

Hands-on 3 Here Why GlobalFilter without order Ordered with order 100 Ensures it runs after RemoveRequestHeader=id-account (default-filters have order 1, 2…); otherwise the header the gateway itself adds would be removed. throw ResponseStatusException 401/503 response written directly Avoids a stack trace in the log for every invalid token and distinguishes "bad token" (401) from "Auth down" (503). new WebClient.builder() on every request one AuthClient with a reused WebClient and a 3 s timeout Fewer objects per request, and the gateway does not hang if Auth stalls. no cache TokenCache (Redis) See Cache.

Uma plataforma de microsserviços para uma loja: o usuário se cadastra, faz login e consulta câmbio entre moedas. Todas as requisições entram por um único ponto (o gateway, atrás de um balanceador Nginx), que valida o token JWT e repassa a identidade do usuário para os serviços.

docs.title: Fluxo de uma requisição autenticada
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Usuário
    participant LB as Nginx
    participant GW as Gateway
    participant R as Redis
    participant A as Auth
    participant S as Serviço (account/exchange)
    U->>LB: GET /accounts (cookie __store_jwt_token)
    LB->>GW: proxy (round robin entre réplicas)
    GW->>GW: remove id-account enviado pelo cliente
    GW->>R: GET gateway:token:sha256(jwt)
    alt cache hit
        R-->>GW: id da conta
    else cache miss
        GW->>A: POST /auth/solve {token}
        A-->>GW: {idAccount} ou 401
        GW->>R: SET ... EX min(5 min, exp do JWT)
    end
    GW->>S: GET /accounts + header id-account
    S-->>U: resposta

docs.title: Contrato da API
docs.text: Combinado entre o grupo (baseado no site do curso, hands-on 1 e 3, e no exercício do Exchange).

docs.title: Gateway
docs.text:
• Lê o cookie __store_jwt_token em toda requisição.
  • Rotas abertas (sem token): POST /auth/register, POST /auth/login, GET /auth/logout.
  • Todo o resto (inclusive /accounts/** e /exchange/**) exige token.
  • Valida chamando POST /auth/solve no Auth e repassa o id no header id-account.
  • /exchanges/** também é aceito e reescrito para /exchange/** (o enunciado usa os dois nomes).

docs.title: Auth (http://auth:8080)
docs.text: Método Rota Entrada Saída POST /auth/register { name, email, password } 200 POST /auth/login { email, password } 200 + Set-Cookie: __store_jwt_token=<jwt> GET /auth/logout — 200, limpa o cookie GET /auth/me header id-account { id, name, email } POST /auth/solve { token } { idAccount } (interno, só o gateway chama) GET /auth/health-check — 200

docs.title: JWT
docs.text:
• Claims: jti = id da conta, sub = nome, email, iss, nbf, exp.
  • Duração: 24 h (JWT_DURATION). Segredo em JWT_SECRET_KEY (variável de ambiente, nunca no código).
  • Cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=None, Path=/.

docs.title: Account (http://account:8080)
docs.text: Método Rota Entrada Saída POST /accounts { name, email, password } 201 GET /accounts — [{ id, name, email }] GET /accounts/{id} — { id, name, email } DELETE /accounts/{id} — 204 POST /accounts/login { email, password } { id, name, email } (interno, o Auth chama) GET /accounts/health-check — 200

docs.title: Exchange (Python)
docs.text: Método Rota Entrada Saída GET /exchange/{from}/{to} header id-account { sell, buy, date, id-account }

docs.title: Decisões
docs.text: Decisão Motivo Nomes dos serviços auth, account, exchange, gateway iguais no compose e no k8s Os Feign clients usam http://account:8080 e http://auth:8080. Só o lb publica porta Gateway e serviços ficam na camada confiável; o header id-account só pode vir do gateway. Cache do token no Redis, chave = SHA-256 do JWT Tira o Auth do caminho de toda requisição sem guardar o token em texto puro. Uma imagem por serviço no GHCR e no ECR (via OIDC, sem chave da AWS no GitHub) O pipeline publica imagens multi-arch (amd64 para o EKS, arm64 para os Macs do grupo).

docs.title: HTTPS (limitação conhecida)
docs.text:
O Auth devolve o token no cookie __store_jwt_token com HttpOnly, Secure e SameSite=None. O navegador só guarda um cookie Secure vindo de HTTPS (ou de localhost), então:

Onde Situação Compose local (http://localhost) Funciona no navegador: localhost conta como origem segura. EKS (http://<elb>.elb.amazonaws.com) O ELB atende só HTTP. Clientes que mandam o cookie no header (curl, scripts/smoke-test.sh, k6) funcionam; o navegador descarta o cookie e as rotas fechadas respondem 401.

Por que não há HTTPS no EKS: um certificado público do ACM exige um domínio validado por DNS, e o grupo não tem domínio; o nome do ELB é da AWS e muda a cada vez que o cluster é recriado. Um certificado autoassinado no Nginx faria o navegador mostrar alerta de segurança, o que não serve para uma loja.

Como ficaria em produção: domínio próprio + certificado do ACM + TLS terminado no balanceador, com anotações no Service lb e redirecionamento de HTTP para HTTPS:

metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: arn:aws:acm:us-east-2:<conta>:certificate/<id>
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports: "443"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: http

Do balanceador para dentro o tráfego segue em HTTP, na rede privada do cluster (camada confiável).

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Git, Java 25 e Maven 3.9+
  • Docker com Docker Compose v2

docs.title: Localmente (Docker Compose)
docs.text:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/pna26/platform.git
cd platform

./scripts/build.sh            # mvn install das interfaces + mvn package dos serviços + cria o .env
docker compose up -d --build  # sobe db, redis, account, auth, exchange, gateway (2 réplicas) e lb
./scripts/smoke-test.sh       # teste ponta a ponta

A plataforma fica em http://localhost:8080. Só o lb (Nginx) publica porta; os demais serviços ficam na rede interna do compose. O Grafana (http://localhost:3000) e o Prometheus (:9090) ficam presos ao 127.0.0.1 — ver Observabilidade.

compose.yaml
# Plataforma completa rodando localmente.
#   ./scripts/build.sh            # compila os jars (interfaces + serviços)
#   docker compose up -d --build  # sobe tudo; entrada em http://localhost:8080
#
# Só o lb (Nginx) publica porta para fora: gateway, auth, account, exchange,
# redis e db ficam na rede interna do compose (camada confiável). Prometheus
# (9090), Grafana (3000), Kafka UI (8089) e Mailpit (8025) ficam presos ao
# 127.0.0.1 da máquina.

name: store

services:

  db:
    image: postgres:17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USER:-store}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-store}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_NAME:-store}
    volumes:
      - db_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}" ]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  # Bottleneck: cache. Guarda token -> id da conta para o gateway não chamar
  # o Auth em toda requisição (ver api/gateway-service/.../TokenCache.java)
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server --appendonly yes
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "redis-cli", "ping" ]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  account:
    build:
      context: ./api/account-service
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      DATABASE_HOST: db
      DATABASE_PORT: 5432
      DATABASE_DB: ${DB_NAME:-store}
      DATABASE_USERNAME: ${DB_USER:-store}
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-store}
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: kafka:9092
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  auth:
    build:
      context: ./api/auth-service
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      # segredo vem do .env (scripts/build.sh gera um aleatório); nunca no código
      JWT_SECRET_KEY: ${JWT_SECRET_KEY:?defina JWT_SECRET_KEY no .env (veja .env.example)}
      JWT_DURATION: ${JWT_DURATION:-86400000}
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    depends_on:
      - account

  gateway:
    build:
      context: ./api/gateway-service
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      REDIS_HOST: redis
      REDIS_PORT: 6379
      # liga/desliga o cache do token (para comparar no teste de carga)
      TOKEN_CACHE_ENABLED: ${TOKEN_CACHE_ENABLED:-true}
      CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: ${CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS:-http://localhost,http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:8080}
    # sem "ports": só é alcançável pelo lb
    deploy:
      replicas: ${GATEWAY_REPLICAS:-2}
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      auth:
        condition: service_started
      account:
        condition: service_started

  # Bottleneck: balanceamento de carga (Nginx na frente das réplicas do gateway)
  lb:
    image: nginx:1.29-alpine
    ports:
      - "${LB_PORT:-8080}:80"
    volumes:
      - ./setup/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
    depends_on:
      - gateway

  # Exchange (Python/FastAPI). Cotação da AwesomeAPI com cache em memória
  # (bottleneck: ver docs/bottlenecks/exchange-cache.md)
  exchange:
    build:
      context: ./api/exchange-service
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      CACHE_TTL: ${EXCHANGE_CACHE_TTL:-30}
      EXCHANGE_API_TOKEN: ${EXCHANGE_API_TOKEN:-}
    deploy:
      replicas: ${EXCHANGE_REPLICAS:-1}

  # Bottleneck: mensageria (docs/bottlenecks/messaging.md), como no Hands-on 7.
  # O account grava a conta e o evento AccountCreated na mesma transação
  # (outbox) e um relay publica no tópico account-events; o notification
  # consome, deduplica pelo eventId e manda o e-mail de boas-vindas ao Mailpit.
  # Kafka 4 de um nó em modo KRaft (broker e controlador no mesmo processo).
  # Só a rede interna do compose fala com ele (sem porta publicada).
  kafka:
    image: apache/kafka:4.3.1
    hostname: kafka
    environment:
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@kafka:9093
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT,CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: 1
      KAFKA_GROUP_INITIAL_REBALANCE_DELAY_MS: 0
      # tópicos criados explicitamente pelo kafka-init (o automático teria 1 partição)
      KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"
      KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: /var/lib/kafka/data
    volumes:
      - kafka_data:/var/lib/kafka/data
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 > /dev/null 2>&1" ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 10s
      start_period: 60s
      retries: 20

  # tarefa única: cria os tópicos e termina. A DLT tem as mesmas 6 partições
  # (o Spring publica a mensagem que falhou no mesmo número de partição)
  kafka-init:
    image: apache/kafka:4.3.1
    depends_on:
      kafka:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint: [ "/bin/sh", "-c" ]
    command:
      - |
        /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --create --if-not-exists           --topic account-events --partitions 6 --replication-factor 1 &&
        /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --create --if-not-exists           --topic account-events-dlt --partitions 6 --replication-factor 1
    restart: "no"

  kafka-ui:
    image: kafbat/kafka-ui:v1.5.0
    environment:
      KAFKA_CLUSTERS_0_NAME: store
      KAFKA_CLUSTERS_0_BOOTSTRAPSERVERS: kafka:9092
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${KAFKA_UI_PORT:-8089}:8080"
    depends_on:
      kafka:
        condition: service_healthy

  # provedor de e-mail falso (SMTP 1025 na rede interna, caixa de entrada web)
  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.31
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${MAILPIT_PORT:-8025}:8025"

  notification:
    build:
      context: ./api/notification-service
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    environment:
      DATABASE_HOST: db
      DATABASE_PORT: 5432
      DATABASE_DB: ${DB_NAME:-store}
      DATABASE_USERNAME: ${DB_USER:-store}
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-store}
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: kafka:9092
      MAIL_HOST: mailpit
      NOTIFY_CONCURRENCY: ${NOTIFY_CONCURRENCY:-3}   # threads consumidoras (no máximo 6 úteis: 6 partições)
      EMAIL_LATENCY: ${EMAIL_LATENCY:-50ms}          # latência simulada do provedor de e-mail
      NOTIFY_IDEMPOTENT: ${NOTIFY_IDEMPOTENT:-true}  # false = sem deduplicação (para ver duplicatas)
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      mailpit:
        condition: service_started
      kafka-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  # Bottleneck: observabilidade (docs/bottlenecks/observability.md).
  # Portas só no 127.0.0.1 do host: ferramentas de operação, não da loja.
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.5.0
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=7d
      # o k6 (scripts/load-test.sh) envia as métricas do teste por remote write
      - --web.enable-remote-write-receiver
    volumes:
      - ./setup/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${PROMETHEUS_PORT:-9090}:9090"
    depends_on:
      - gateway
      - exchange

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:12.1.0
    environment:
      PROMETHEUS_URL: http://prometheus:9090
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED: "false"
      GF_DASHBOARDS_DEFAULT_HOME_DASHBOARD_PATH: /var/lib/grafana/dashboards/store.json
      GF_ANALYTICS_REPORTING_ENABLED: "false"
    volumes:
      - ./setup/grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./setup/grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${GRAFANA_PORT:-3000}:3000"
    depends_on:
      - prometheus

volumes:
  db_data:
  kafka_data:
  redis_data:
  prometheus_data:
  grafana_data:

O .env é criado pelo scripts/build.sh a partir do .env.example, com um JWT_SECRET_KEY aleatório (openssl rand -base64 32). Ele nunca vai para o git.

docs.title: Exemplo de uso
docs.text:
# cadastro e login (o cookie fica no arquivo cookies.txt)
curl -X POST localhost:8080/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ana","email":"ana@store.com","password":"123456"}'
curl -c cookies.txt -X POST localhost:8080/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ana@store.com","password":"123456"}'

# rotas protegidas (o curl só reenvia cookie Secure em HTTPS, então mandamos o header)
TOKEN=$(awk '/__store_jwt_token/ {print $7}' cookies.txt)
curl -H "Cookie: __store_jwt_token=$TOKEN" localhost:8080/auth/me
curl -H "Cookie: __store_jwt_token=$TOKEN" localhost:8080/accounts

docs.title: Smoke test
docs.text:
O scripts/smoke-test.sh é o mesmo que roda no CI (workflow integration). Ele confere:

  • cadastro, login (cookie HttpOnly), /auth/me, /accounts, /exchange/USD/BRL e logout;
  • 401 sem token, com token inválido e com id-account forjado;
  • que pelo menos 2 réplicas do gateway responderam (balanceamento);
  • que o token ficou em cache no Redis;
  • que /gateway/actuator/prometheus não fica exposto pelo lb.
scripts/smoke-test.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Teste ponta a ponta da plataforma rodando (compose local ou EKS):
#   ./scripts/smoke-test.sh                       # http://localhost:8080
#   BASE_URL=http://<elb-da-aws> ./scripts/smoke-test.sh
# Confere o contrato da API, o 401 sem token, o header id-account forjado,
# o balanceamento entre réplicas e o cache do token no Redis.
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8080}"
EMAIL="smoke+$(date +%s)$RANDOM@store.test"
PASS="senha-forte-123"
fail() { echo "FALHOU: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok() { echo "ok  - $*"; }
status() { curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$@"; }

echo ">> esperando o gateway em $BASE_URL"
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  [ "$(status "$BASE_URL/health-check")" = "200" ] && break
  sleep 2
  [ "$i" = 60 ] && fail "gateway não respondeu"
done
ok "gateway no ar"

# o auth/account podem demorar um pouco mais que o gateway para subir
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  code=$(status -X POST "$BASE_URL/auth/register" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"name\":\"Smoke Test\",\"email\":\"$EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$PASS\"}")
  case "$code" in 200|201) break ;; esac
  sleep 3
  [ "$i" = 60 ] && fail "POST /auth/register respondeu $code"
done
ok "POST /auth/register ($code)"

headers=$(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST "$BASE_URL/auth/login" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"email\":\"$EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$PASS\"}")
echo "$headers" | head -1 | grep -q ' 200' || fail "POST /auth/login: $(echo "$headers" | head -1)"
TOKEN=$(echo "$headers" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^[Ss]et-[Cc]ookie: __store_jwt_token=\([^;]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)
[ -n "$TOKEN" ] || fail "login não devolveu o cookie __store_jwt_token"
echo "$headers" | grep -qi 'set-cookie:.*HttpOnly' || fail "cookie sem HttpOnly"
ok "POST /auth/login devolveu o cookie __store_jwt_token (HttpOnly)"

COOKIE="Cookie: __store_jwt_token=$TOKEN"

[ "$(status "$BASE_URL/accounts")" = "401" ] || fail "GET /accounts sem token deveria ser 401"
ok "GET /accounts sem token -> 401"

[ "$(status -H 'id-account: forjado' "$BASE_URL/accounts")" = "401" ] || fail "id-account forjado abriu a rota"
ok "header id-account forjado sem token -> 401"

[ "$(status -H "Cookie: __store_jwt_token=token.invalido.x" "$BASE_URL/accounts")" = "401" ] || fail "token inválido deveria ser 401"
ok "token inválido -> 401"

me=$(curl -s -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/auth/me")
echo "$me" | grep -q "$EMAIL" || fail "GET /auth/me: $me"
ok "GET /auth/me devolve a conta logada"

ID=$(echo "$me" | sed -n 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
# RBAC (bottleneck de autorização): conta nova é USER
[ "$(status -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/accounts/$ID")" = "200" ] || fail "GET /accounts/{próprio id}"
ok "GET /accounts/{próprio id} -> 200"
[ "$(status -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/accounts")" = "403" ] || fail "USER listou todas as contas"
ok "RBAC: USER em GET /accounts (listar todos) -> 403"
[ "$(status -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/accounts/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")" = "403" ] || fail "USER viu conta de outro"
ok "RBAC: USER em GET /accounts/{outro id} -> 403"
[ "$(status -X DELETE -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/accounts/$ID")" = "403" ] || fail "USER apagou conta"
ok "RBAC: USER em DELETE /accounts/{id} -> 403"

[ "$(status "$BASE_URL/exchange/USD/BRL")" = "401" ] || fail "GET /exchange sem token deveria ser 401"
ok "GET /exchange/USD/BRL sem token -> 401"

# o exchange depende de uma API externa: 503 (fora do ar/limite) vira só aviso
ex=$(curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/exchange/USD/BRL")
code=$(echo "$ex" | tail -1); body=$(echo "$ex" | sed '$d')
case "$code" in
  200)
    echo "$body" | grep -q '"sell"' && echo "$body" | grep -q '"buy"' || fail "GET /exchange/USD/BRL: $body"
    echo "$body" | grep -q "\"id-account\":\"$ID\"" || fail "exchange não recebeu o id-account do gateway: $body"
    ok "GET /exchange/USD/BRL -> 200 com sell/buy e o id-account do usuário" ;;
  503) echo "aviso - exchange respondeu 503 (API de câmbio externa indisponível)" ;;
  *) fail "GET /exchange/USD/BRL respondeu $code: $body" ;;
esac
[ "$(status -H "$COOKIE" "$BASE_URL/exchanges/USD/XX")" = "400" ] || fail "/exchanges/{from}/{to} (apelido) deveria chegar no exchange"
ok "GET /exchanges/... (apelido) chega no exchange"

hosts=$(for i in $(seq 1 12); do curl -s "$BASE_URL/health-check"; echo; done | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$hosts" -ge 2 ]; then ok "balanceamento: $hosts réplicas diferentes do gateway responderam"
else echo "aviso - só 1 réplica do gateway respondeu (GATEWAY_REPLICAS=1?)"; fi

if command -v docker >/dev/null && docker compose ps redis >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  keys=$(docker compose exec -T redis redis-cli --scan --pattern 'gateway:token:*' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$keys" -ge 1 ] || fail "nenhum token em cache no redis"
  ok "cache: $keys token(s) em cache no Redis (chave = SHA-256 do JWT)"
fi

[ "$(status "$BASE_URL/gateway/actuator/prometheus")" = "404" ] || fail "métricas não deveriam ser públicas"
ok "/gateway/actuator/prometheus bloqueado no lb"

logout=$(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "$BASE_URL/auth/logout")
echo "$logout" | grep -qi 'set-cookie: __store_jwt_token=;' || fail "logout não limpou o cookie"
ok "GET /auth/logout limpa o cookie"

echo ">> smoke test passou"

docs.title: Variações úteis
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --scale gateway=4      # mais réplicas (o Nginx descobre sozinho)
TOKEN_CACHE_ENABLED=false docker compose up -d gateway   # desliga o cache (comparar no teste de carga)
docker compose up -d --scale exchange=3                  # mais réplicas do exchange
docker compose down -v                                    # derruba tudo e apaga os volumes

docs.title: No EKS
docs.text:
O deploy no EKS é feito pelo pipeline (CI/CD): cada serviço aplica o seu k8s/ e o repositório platform aplica a infra compartilhada (k8s/lb.yaml e k8s/redis.yaml). Para aplicar manualmente:

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name <cluster> --region <região>
kubectl create namespace store
kubectl apply -n store -f k8s/                         # lb (Nginx + LoadBalancer) e redis
kubectl apply -n store -f api/gateway-service/k8s/     # gateway
kubectl get svc lb -n store                            # endereço público do ELB
BASE_URL=http://<endereço-do-elb> ./scripts/smoke-test.sh

docs.title: Esta documentação
docs.text: Feita com MkDocs + Material for MkDocs, a partir do template de entrega do professor. As páginas incluem o código direto dos submódulos (--8<-- "api/<serviço>/..."), então o que aparece aqui é sempre o código da versão referenciada pelo repositório principal.
